title: Superellipsoid geometry with analytic normals
purpose: Build Barr superellipsoids for three.js, from rounded cubes and cushions through ellipsoids to octahedra and star prisms, with three radii, two shape exponents, analytic normals, UVs, the inside-outside function and the exact volume, from a typed-array generator that also runs in Node.

engine.name: webgl2_browser
engine.notes: superellipsoidData, superellipsoidVolume and superellipsoidImplicit need no three.js; createSuperellipsoidGeometry takes three.js as THREE; only 0.186.1 was run.

exports.name: superellipsoidData
exports.summary: The superellipsoid as typed arrays on a latitude-longitude grid, triangles counter-clockwise from outside.

exports.name: createSuperellipsoidGeometry
exports.summary: The same data in a BufferGeometry with an index and computed bounds.

exports.name: superellipsoidVolume
exports.signature: superellipsoidVolume(radiusX, radiusY, radiusZ, exponentY, exponentXZ) -> number
exports.summary: Exact volume 2 a b c e1 e2 B(e1/2 + 1, e1) B(e2/2, e2/2).

exports.name: superellipsoidImplicit
exports.summary: Barr's inside-outside function: below 1 inside, 1 on the surface, above 1 outside.

options.name: exponentY
options.meaning: Barr's epsilon 1, the north-south roundness: near 0 square, 1 round, 2 pointed, above 2 pinched.

options.name: exponentXZ
options.meaning: Barr's epsilon 2, the east-west roundness of the horizontal cross-section.

outputs.index_type: Uint16Array up to 65535 vertices, else Uint32Array

limits: A latitude-longitude grid: vertices crowd at the poles and the seam and pole rows repeat for UVs, as in SphereGeometry. Very small exponents bunch the grid against the box edges, so near-cubes need many segments. Exponents above 2 make concave shapes with cusps where the surface has no normal; there the ellipsoid normal of the point is used, which is an approximation. UVs follow the angles, not arc length, so textures stretch on boxy shapes. The mesh volume is slightly under superellipsoidVolume for convex shapes. Only three.js 0.186.1 was run, in headless Chrome on SwiftShader WebGL 2.
technique_references: Barr superquadric ellipsoid with signed-power trigonometric parametrization
Analytic normal from the dual exponents 2 - e
Volume through Beta functions, with log-gamma from Stirling's series
